To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
genetic selection for feed efficiency in pigs is associated with changes in the protein profile of mitochondria isolated from the liver and longissimus doris muscle.
genetic selection for residual feed intake tends to result in changes in the mitochondria protein profiles in liver and longissimus dori muscle.
mitochondria isolated from the liver of pigs that are genetically selected for RFI have increased levels of ATP synthase and HSP60 and HSP70.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of feed efficiency in pigs.
the identification of molecular markers associated with differences in growth efficiency in pigs.
the identification and validation of genes associated with RFI and the elucidation of the mechanisms underlying these associations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mitochondrial proteome is altered in pigs selected for RFI, but that the changes are more related to genetic selection than to the RFI phenotypes.
genetic selection for feed efficiency in pigs results in a change in mitochondria protein profile in liver and skeletal muscle, and this is associated with changes in posttranslational modification.
genetic selection of RFI is associated with changes in mitochondrial protein profile, but that these changes are not specific for RFI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mitochondrial proteome is altered in pigs divergent selected for residual feed efficiency.
the mitochondrial protein profile of the liver is altered by genetic selection for RFD.
selection for RFI is associated with a mitochondrial protein profile that differs in a consistent manner from that in pigs not selected for this trait.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondria proteins are altered in the high RFI line, but these differences are not consistent between tissues.
the mitochondrial proteome is not altered by RFI selection.
